identity.title: An Online Adaptive Sampling Algorithm for Stochastic Difference-of-convex Optimization with Time-varying Distributions

problem.claim: Solve stochastic nonsmooth difference-of-convex optimization when the data distribution changes over time.

contributions.claim: An online adaptive sampling algorithm using only current-distribution data and separate sampling rates for convex and concave components.
A convergence analysis establishing almost-sure subsequential convergence to DC critical points under suitable distribution-convergence conditions.
A pointwise O(√(p/n)) convergence rate, up to logarithmic factors, for sample-average approximations of subdifferential mappings.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors identify separate component-wise sampling rates as a novel design guided by theory and present the subdifferential-mapping rate as a novel result of independent interest.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report almost-sure subsequential convergence to DC critical points when the distributions satisfy proper convergence conditions.
The authors report that the sample-size requirement matches static-distribution results for smooth problems or cases with a measurable subgradient selector.
Numerical experiments are reported to confirm efficiency and effectiveness on stochastic nonsmooth problems.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper proposes online adaptive sampling for stochastic nonsmooth DC optimization with time-varying distributions.
The method uses only current data and assigns distinct adaptive sampling rates to the convex and concave components.
Under suitable distribution-convergence conditions, the method is reported to converge subsequentially almost surely to DC critical points.
The reported sample-size requirement matches specified static-distribution benchmarks, supported by a new subdifferential-mapping convergence rate.
Numerical experiments report efficiency and effectiveness for stochastic nonsmooth problems.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a distinct algorithmic choice—separate sampling rates for convex and concave terms—to the theoretical analysis.

lessons.interpretation: A method’s design rationale can be made more persuasive by explicitly connecting it to the theorem or rate that motivates it.
lessons.application: When presenting an adaptive algorithm, state which analytical asymmetry motivates each separately tuned component.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when component-specific tuning is heuristic or lacks a corresponding analytical role.

source_observation.claim: The abstract states a convergence rate together with its dependence on dimension, sample size, and logarithmic-factor qualification.

lessons.interpretation: Including scaling variables and caveats makes a quantitative claim more interpretable.
lessons.application: State rates with their key parameters and explicitly mark omitted factors or regimes.
lessons.exception: Do not foreground a rate when the relevant assumptions or evaluation setting are unavailable.

unknowns: The specific conditions required for distribution convergence and the exact meaning of subsequential convergence are not given.
The sample-size requirement and matching constants or regimes are unspecified.
The numerical datasets, baselines, metrics, and experimental results are not reported.
